gap: No result ChatGPT got states any named reviewer's test of gaming mic quality. That leaves two things unsaid: SoundGuys' 2,324-vote listener poll rated the HyperX Cloud III's boom mic 4 or 5 out of 5 for 77% of voters (52% Good, 25% Perfect), and LANOC found that the Maono PD200X dynamic desk mic still picked up keyboard and mouse at full gain from 19 in and 27 in away.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results or catalog cards, so no rival page was there to compare. Its answer is a generic table ('Decent' vs 'Usually better' voice quality) with no reviewer, no measurement and no named product. Any named, dated test figure is new. None of these findings decides the pick, though, because RTINGS keeps its lab mic numbers (LFE, HFE, SpNR) behind a membership lock, and no source I could open had measured noise-floor or frequency-response numbers for the desk mics.
decides: The 'headset is enough' advice holds up: SoundGuys listeners rated a mid-price wired boom mic (Cloud III) Good or Perfect 77% of the time. A dynamic desk mic only beats a headset on keyboard noise if it sits close and the gain is turned down. At full gain from about 19 in, LANOC still heard keys and static on the PD200X. This should change our page's 'Low' keyboard-noise cell for the PD200XS to 'Low only when 2 to 4 in. from the mouth with gain below max'. Podcastage found that the ModMic USB, a clip-on for headphones you already own, sounds not much better than a standard gaming headset. That weakens the 'already have good headphones, add a ModMic' route for anyone who wants better-than-headset voice quality: they should buy a standalone mic instead.

findings.label: SoundGuys reader poll, 'How does the microphone sound to you?'
findings.source_title: HyperX Cloud III review - SoundGuys (Riley Ballantyne)
findings.note: A listener poll on SoundGuys' recorded mic samples, not an instrument measurement. 52% + 25% = 77% voted 4 or 5. Reviewer's text: 'decent as far as gaming headsets go', 'frequency response is relatively flat'. Review first published 2023-06-14, updated 2025-01-29.

findings.label: RTINGS test bench and mic measurement access
findings.value: Test Bench 1.6 (converted 2023-11-23); mic LFE, HFE, weighted THD and SpNR values locked to members
findings.source_title: HyperX Cloud III Headphones Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Opened through a text renderer because the page loads by script. Every mic figure shows 'Locked', so no RTINGS number is quoted. Review published 2023-09-12, last updated 2026-05-04.

findings.label: LANOC desk test of the PD200X (the same mic sold in the PD200XS set)
findings.value: Picked up keyboard and mouse and a little background static at full gain, with the keyboard 19 in and the mouse 27 in away
findings.source_title: Maono PD200X USB/XLR Dynamic Microphone - LANOC (Wes Compton)
findings.note: Quotes: 'It did pick up my keyboard and mouse, especially at full volume'; 'a bit of a background static when set to full volume'. Distances are the reviewer's own setup. Gain was at 100% (spec range 0 to +42 dB). The article is dated 14 June and its image paths suggest 2023. MSRP at review was $79.99.

findings.label: Podcastage test settings
findings.value: Interface gain 30 dB, plus 6 dB boost in post (16-bit/48 kHz USB)
findings.source_title: Fifine AM8 Review / Test - Podcastage (Bandrew Scott)
findings.note: The gain the reviewer needed for normal speech level, as written on the page ('1:30dB', +6 dB in post). The page gives no noise-floor figure. Price at review was 'around $50'. Verdict: 'sounds pretty darn good especially considering the price', recommended only 'kind of' because of the mount. The page shows Dec 10 with no year.

findings.label: APH Networks keyboard and mouse pickup test
findings.value: Picked up a slight amount of keyboard and mouse clicks, heard as a deeper resonant thud rather than high clicks
findings.source_title: FIFINE AmpliGame AM8 Review (Page 3 of 4) - APH Networks
findings.note: A listening test, not a measurement. The page shows no byline or date.

findings.label: Podcastage verdict after polar-pattern and background-noise tests
findings.value: Mics 'do not provide audio that sounds much better than a standard gaming headset'
findings.source_title: Antlion ModMic USB and ModMic Uni Review - Podcastage (Bandrew Scott)
findings.note: A named judgement after timed polar-pattern and background-noise test segments. The page gives no numbers. It adds that for podcasts or high-quality streams 'you'd be better served with a standalone mic'. The page shows Jan 28 with no year.

unsourced: RTINGS mic numbers for the HyperX Cloud III (Recording Quality LFE/HFE, weighted harmonic distortion, Speech + Pink Noise and Speech + Subway SpNR, noise isolation): the page opened, but every value is locked to members.
Any lab mic measurement for the EKSA E900 Pro: RTINGS has no review, the Igor's Lab test page returned 403, and the other reviews I found (Techaeris, iMore, mictests user posts) give no figures.
A measured noise floor or frequency response for the FIFINE AM8: the TechPowerUp single-page review returned 403, and Podcastage and APH Networks give no noise-floor value.

A measured self-noise or frequency-response figure for the Maono PD200X/PD200XS: LANOC, GameSpace (graph image only, no numbers in the text) and Micpedia (empty fields) have none. A Julian Krause measurement did not turn up.
A measured noise or frequency figure for the ModMic USB: the Tom's Hardware review body did not render, and Podcastage gives no numbers.
Any named review or measurement of the Maono DGM20 GamerWave: none found within the tool budget.
